name: Tay Ninh
provinceNote: Resolution 202/2025/QH15, passed 12 June 2025, joined old Long An and old Tây Ninh and kept the name Tây Ninh: 8,536.44 km² and 3,254,170 people, beside Đồng Nai, Đồng Tháp, Ho Chi Minh City, and Cambodia. The new provincial government started 1 July 2025. Resolution 1682 counts 96 communes, 82 xã and 14 phường. This night is the Holy See and Ba Den. The former Long An towns are a separate trip.
dotReason: The noon service and the next morning’s cable are the reason to stay.
summary: A province for the Cao Dai Holy See noon service and Ba Den mountain. Watch the noon rite in the courtyard, then ride the cable up Ba Den the next morning. Two days and one night is the stay from Ho Chi Minh City.
getThere: About 100 km, about 110 km to Ba Den, or about 90 km to more than 100 km from Ho Chi Minh City. No train.
seoTitle: Tay Ninh travel guide — Cao Dai noon service and Ba Den
seoDescription: Stay for the Cao Dai noon service and Ba Den the next morning. Ho Chi Minh City is about 100 km, about 110 km, or about 90 km to more than 100 km.
intro: You come for the Cao Dai Holy See noon service and Ba Den mountain. You are in the courtyard of the Cao Dai Holy See at noon, under the long pale front, the bell tower, and the drum tower. The Divine Eye is a detail on that front. Stay the night in phường Tân Ninh, the old city centre, if that noon service and the first cable up Ba Den the next morning are the trip. Sleep nearer the gate in phường Bình Minh if you want that first cabin. The night is the forecourt at the 18:00 service, in phường Long Hoa, or the mountain after 17:00, when the operator posts a lower cable fare. Go back to Ho Chi Minh City if the city is the trip, and do not build the night around Cu Chi. The provincial homepage puts Ho Chi Minh City about 100 km away and offers 2 days and 1 night. The national mountain card says about 110 km northwest, measured to Ba Den. From Tân Sơn Nhất the operator says about 90 km to more than 100 km to the city centre, and a first stop at the mountain that can exceed 110 km. That page’s drive is about 2.5 to 3 hours. A 2018 article says about 100 km from Sài Gòn to the valley, then about 50 km on tỉnh lộ 782 to the old town. Keep all of those distances.

Walk the court and look into the prayer hall at a service. The plan is a dragon-horse. The mountain board gives the hall at 97.5 m by 22 m. The ward page says twelve carved gates. Noon is the service the provincial card tells you to see. Dress is modest on that card. Shoes come off. Men take the right door. Women take the left door. Daily services are also 0:00, 6:00, and 18:00. The page calls the four together cúng tứ thời. The Bình Dương tourism page allows about 60 minutes. Tây Ninh pages do not give a visit length, so there is no second figure. The temple is about 4 km southeast of the old city, in phường Long Hoa. The footer on the mountain board, khu phố Ninh Phú, phường Bình Minh, is the mountain office. Do not paste it onto the temple.

The mountain board says work started in 1931, was completed on 24 January 1947, and was inaugurated on 1 February 1955. The provincial card, the ward page, and the Bình Dương page say work started in 1933. The ward page says the building was completed in 1947 and inaugurated in 1955. The provincial card says the work was finished in 1955. Keep both 1947 and 1955. The ward page gives grounds of more than 1 km² and, on the same page, nearly 100 ha. The Bình Dương page says about 1 km². That ward page also says 3,027 stars on the canopy and 3,072 globes. Chí Tôn day is the 9th of lunar January on the mountain board, and the 8th of lunar January on the ward page, which also says more than 30,000 people. Keep both days. On 25 September 2026 the Mother Goddess flower procession was at 18:30 and the great rite at 22:00.

Ba Den is the other half of the stay. The tourism card puts the mountain a little more than 10 km from the city centre. The biodiversity page puts it 11 km northeast of the old town. The height on the mountain board, the tourism card, and the national card is 986 m, called nóc nhà Nam Bộ, with núi Heo at 335 m and núi Phụng at 660 m on the mountain board. The national card says about 24 km² for the complex. The biodiversity page says nearly 2,000 ha for the 1986 landscape reserve, Decision 194/CT of 9 August 1986. Those areas are not averaged. The national card also names a 1,200 m cable and a slide of 1,190 m up and 1,700 m down. The 2026 operator pages name three lines, Vân Sơn to the summit, Chùa Hang toward the Bà temples, and Tâm An, and do not repeat those lengths. On the summit the mountain board describes a 72 m copper Phật Bà of 170 tons, and a sandstone Di Lặc 36 m high, 45 m wide, of 6,688 blocks. Ba Den Station is given as 10,959 m² on that page. Those statue and station figures are one source. Recognition is Decision 100-VH/QĐ on the mountain board and 100/VH-QĐ on the biodiversity page, both dated 21 January 1989. The war unit is Hậu cần 82 on the mountain board and Hậu cần 32 on the biodiversity page. Liên đội 7 is on both. The caves on the mountain are not the Cu Chi tunnels.

The clock in force on 22 October 2026 is the 28 September 2026 notice, until a later notice. Monday to Friday, Vân Sơn and Chùa Hang run 06:00–20:30. Tâm An does not run those days. The spiritual area is 06:30–20:00. Saturday, Vân Sơn and Chùa Hang run 05:30–21:00, Tâm An 06:30–19:00, and the spiritual area 06:00–20:30. Sunday, Vân Sơn and Chùa Hang run 05:30–20:30, Tâm An 06:30–19:00, and the spiritual area 06:00–20:00. The gate is open one hour before the cable and one hour after. The buffet is 10:00–15:00. An earlier operator article says 6:00–20:00 on Monday and Friday and 5:30–21:00 on weekends and holidays, and does not name Tuesday to Thursday. Keep both clocks. That earlier article says the last ride up is often 30 minutes before close. The 28 September notice does not repeat that half hour. Weather can stop the cable.

From 16 February 2026 through 3 May 2026, and again from 28 September 2026 through 31 December 2026, the operator gives a gate of 10,000 đồng for an adult and 5,000 for a child. Vân Sơn is 450,000 and 350,000. Chùa Hang round trip is 250,000 and 150,000. Tâm An is 450,000 and 350,000. Under 1 m is free. From 1 m to under 1.4 m is the child fare. From 1.4 m is adult. After 17:00, on the 28 September–31 December notice only, Vân Sơn is 300,000 and 200,000, Chùa Hang round trip is 150,000 and 100,000, and Tâm An is 300,000 and 200,000. The June window of 18–26 June 2026 gives a Chùa Bà cable of 125,000 and a summit combo of 450,000 and 350,000. That window is closed. Do not pay it in October. Its 24–27 September 2026 notice listed a tube slide at 07:30–18:00 and a cable at 07:30–16:00.

Hồ Dầu Tiếng is the sunset once the temple and the mountain are planned. The mountain board says “diện tích mặt nước 27 km”, then a catchment of 27,000 ha and up to 1.58 billion m³. The operator says 270 km² and 1.58 billion m³. The national card says 27,000 ha and 1.5 billion m³. The figure “27 km” stands as written. Keep both 1.5 billion and 1.58 billion. The shore the national card names is about 20 km from the city. Ma Thiên Lãnh is a walk between Ba Den, Phụng, and Heo to a green stone lake on the west foot of núi Heo. It is a quarry pool in the write-ups, not a swim, and the 2018 article says people carried lunch because there was no food stall. Chùa Gò Kén, also Chùa Thiền Lâm, is the temple the homepage calls more than 100 years old and the earliest built in Tây Ninh. Do not swap it with the Holy See or with Chùa Bà on the mountain. Gạo Nàng Thơm Chợ Đào, thanh long Đức Hòa, rượu đế Gò Đen, cá lóc nướng trui, lẩu mắm, and khô cá lóc belong to the old Long An half. They are not lunch at the Holy See.
gettingAround: The nearest airport is Tân Sơn Nhất, in Ho Chi Minh City. The operator’s transfer page starts the road there. The provincial tourism homepage does not name a passenger airport inside Tây Ninh. No rail station was recorded on the tourism homepage or on that road page. Do not plan a train.

The operator leaves Tân Sơn Nhất toward Cộng Hòa, then Quốc lộ 22, through Trảng Bàng and Gò Dầu, into the city, and on to the mountain if that is the first stop. A 2018 article uses Quốc lộ 22A to the Trảng Bàng junction, then tỉnh lộ 782. Keep both road numbers. The provincial homepage says about 100 km from Ho Chi Minh City. The national card says about 110 km northwest, to Ba Den. The operator says about 90 km to more than 100 km from the airport to the city centre, a first stop at the mountain that can exceed 110 km, and a drive of about 2.5 to 3 hours. The 2018 article says about 100 km from Sài Gòn to the valley, then about 50 km on tỉnh lộ 782. That 50 km is not the operator’s 90 km to more than 100 km. A coach fare, a first bus, and an official station door were not on a provincial timetable. Old phường 2 is inside phường Tân Ninh from 1 July 2025.

The Holy See is about 4 km southeast of the old city, in phường Long Hoa. The mountain is a little more than 10 km from the city centre, and 11 km northeast on the biodiversity page. From 1 July 2025 the old city centre is phường Tân Ninh, old Long Hoa stays inside phường Long Hoa, and old Thạnh Tân and old Ninh Sơn are inside phường Bình Minh. The mountain office says khu phố Ninh Phú, phường Bình Minh. That line is not the temple’s door. On the way in, Trảng Bàng sits on Quốc lộ 22. The town page names địa đạo An Thới and does not give a fee, an hour, or what a visitor does. That is not the Cu Chi site.

stayAreas.name: Tân Ninh
stayAreas.summary: Sleep in phường Tân Ninh, the old city centre, when the noon service and the 18:00 rite are the point. No hotel brand is a pick.

stayAreas.name: Bình Minh
stayAreas.summary: Sleep nearer the mountain gate in phường Bình Minh when you want the first cable. The gate address is khu phố Ninh Phú. No hotel brand is a pick.

eat: The meal on the way in is bánh tráng phơi sương at Trảng Bàng, rolled with boiled pork or boiled young beef. Bánh canh, bò tơ, and muối tôm are the other Trảng Bàng plates. Bún Xiêm Lo is the border bowl. Lẩu mắm, Nàng Thơm Chợ Đào rice, and dried snakehead are the old Long An half, not lunch at the Holy See.
interestsBody: Dining is the Trảng Bàng roll, bánh canh, and bò tơ on the way in. Muối tôm is the jar. Bún Xiêm Lo is the border bowl. The old Long An half is a different meal.
The Holy See is the Cao Dai central temple in phường Long Hoa, with four daily services. Noon is the one visitors are pointed to. It is not a pagoda row, and it is not a wing of the Cu Chi tunnels.

Ba Den, at 986 m, is the cable day. The lake at dusk is Hồ Dầu Tiếng. Ma Thiên Lãnh is the walk on the same hills. Chùa Gò Kén is a short stop on the plain if a ward, a fee, and an hour are posted when you arrive.

Sheets from khu phố Lộc Du, and muối tôm on the homepage’s specialty line, are what you carry. No mall and no boutique street were named. Zone-I points on the mountain, including Liên đội 7, are the war layer. Hậu cần 82 and Hậu cần 32 are both given. This is not Cu Chi.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: The Trảng Bàng roll, bánh canh, and bò tơ.
body: Sit in khu phố Gia Huỳnh for bánh tráng phơi sương and bánh canh. The yards are khu phố Lộc Du. Bò tơ is along Quốc lộ 22, in phường Trảng Bàng and phường An Tịnh. The provincial tourism center marks that beef as lunch.

The same center speaks of bún Xiêm Lo at breakfast or at lunch, and does not name the commune. Mãng cầu Bà Đen is the fruit at the mountain. Lẩu mắm and Nàng Thơm Chợ Đào rice stay on the old Long An half.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Bánh tráng phơi sương at Trảng Bàng, then bánh canh and bò tơ.

interestGroups.title: The Holy See
interestGroups.summary: The noon service in the court, and the 18:00 rite if you are staying.
body: Come for the courtyard and the prayer hall. Noon is the service the provincial card tells visitors to see. The other daily hours are 0:00, 6:00, and 18:00. Shoes come off. Men take the right door. Women take the left door. Dress is modest. The Bình Dương page allows about 60 minutes. Tây Ninh pages do not give a second length.

The mountain board puts Chí Tôn on the 9th of lunar January. The ward page puts it on the 8th, and says more than 30,000 people. Keep both days. The grounds are about 4 km southeast of the old city. The mountain office address in phường Bình Minh is not this door.

cards.title: Cao Dai Holy See
cards.summary: The court at noon. About 60 minutes on the Bình Dương page.

faqs.q: Should I stay the night in Tay Ninh or come back to Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Stay if you want the noon service and the first cable the next morning. The provincial homepage offers 2 days and 1 night and says about 100 km. The national card says about 110 km to Ba Den. From Tân Sơn Nhất the operator says about 90 km to more than 100 km to the city centre, a mountain-first road that can exceed 110 km, and a drive of about 2.5 to 3 hours. A 2018 article says about 100 km to the valley, then about 50 km. Go back the same day only if Ho Chi Minh City is the trip. Cu Chi is not this night.

faqs.q: Is there a ticket for the Holy See, and how long is the visit?
faqs.a: The Bình Dương tourism page allows about 60 minutes. Tây Ninh pages do not give a visit length. The temple is about 4 km southeast of the old city. Shoes come off. Men take the right door. Women take the left door.

faqs.q: Which Ba Den cable clock applies, and what does the ride cost?
faqs.a: On 22 October 2026 the notice in force is the 28 September 2026 clock, until a later notice: weekdays Vân Sơn and Chùa Hang 06:00–20:30, Saturday 05:30–21:00, Sunday 05:30–20:30. An earlier article says 6:00–20:00 on Monday and Friday and 5:30–21:00 on weekends and holidays, and does not name Tuesday to Thursday. The round-trip cables on the September–December notice are Vân Sơn 450,000 and 350,000, Chùa Hang 250,000 and 150,000, Tâm An 450,000 and 350,000, plus a gate of 10,000 and 5,000. After 17:00 those cables are lower on that notice. The 18–26 June festival prices are a closed window.

season.label: Dry Dec–Apr
season.note: December to April is the easier time on Hồ Dầu Tiếng, at dawn and dusk, and the dry walk at Ma Thiên Lãnh. August to November the valley path is slippery. Lunar January is the spring festival on Ba Den, from the 4th through the end of that lunar month. Lunar days 4, 5, and 6 of the fifth month are the Bà pilgrimage, and those days fill the cable. In 2026 The figure windows were 18–20 June, 18–22 June, and 18–21 June. The cable clock can change in bad weather.
